note: Holdout #5, written 2026-10-25 09:25 PDT before any run. Expected verdicts from Cochrane, WHO, CDC, NIH/NCI/NTP, USPSTF, NICE, IARC/JECFA, ACOG and landmark trials. also_ok decided in advance. harmful: shown verdicts that could hurt a reader. None of these claims appear in the regression set, the safety set, the tests, or holdouts #1 to #4.

claims.claim: The rotavirus vaccine protects babies from severe diarrhea
claims.basis: Cochrane (Soares-Weiser 2019, updated Bergman 2021): rotavirus vaccines prevent about 80 to 85% of severe rotavirus diarrhea in low-mortality countries and about 60% in high-mortality countries, high-certainty, and also cut severe diarrhea from any cause; WHO has recommended it in every national schedule since 2009.

claims.claim: Cognitive behavioral therapy helps people with insomnia
claims.basis: American College of Physicians guideline (Qaseem 2016): CBT for insomnia is first-line for chronic insomnia, strong recommendation, moderate-quality evidence; meta-analysis of trials (Trauer 2015) found people fall asleep about 19 minutes sooner; the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (2021) and NICE also recommend it.

claims.claim: Pelvic floor exercises reduce urinary incontinence in women
claims.basis: Cochrane (Dumoulin 2018, 31 trials): pelvic floor muscle training cures or improves urinary incontinence in women compared with no treatment, most clearly for stress incontinence; NICE (2019) recommends supervised training for at least 3 months as first-line treatment.

claims.claim: The shingles vaccine prevents shingles in older adults
claims.basis: Cochrane (Gagliardi 2019, updated 2023): zoster vaccines prevent shingles in older adults; the recombinant vaccine cut shingles by about 90 to 97% in the ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 trials (Lal 2015, Cunningham 2016); CDC/ACIP recommends it for all adults 50 and over.

claims.claim: Giving babies peanut foods early lowers the risk of peanut allergy
claims.basis: LEAP trial (Du Toit 2015): early peanut introduction cut peanut allergy by about 80% in high-risk infants; NIAID addendum guidelines (2017) and later AAP advice recommend it; systematic review (Ierodiakonou 2016, JAMA): moderate-certainty benefit (risk ratio about 0.3). Strongest in high-risk infants, so a narrower reading is fair.

claims.claim: Selenium supplements prevent cancer
claims.basis: Cochrane (Vinceti 2018, selenium for preventing cancer): high-quality trials show no reduction in cancer risk, with possible increases in type 2 diabetes and high-grade prostate cancer; SELECT (Lippman 2009, about 35,000 men) found no prevention; observational links are very low certainty.

claims.claim: Saw palmetto relieves the symptoms of an enlarged prostate
claims.basis: Cochrane (Tacklind 2012, 32 trials, 5,666 men): saw palmetto was no better than placebo for urinary symptoms or flow, even at double and triple doses; the CAMUS trial (Barry 2011) agrees; NCCIH says it has not been shown to work.

claims.claim: Vitamin D supplements prevent falls in older adults
claims.basis: USPSTF 2018 grade D against vitamin D to prevent falls in community-dwelling adults 65 and over, and its 2024 draft keeps grade D for adults 60 and over (20 trials, pooled risk ratio 0.99); Cochrane (Gillespie 2012) found no overall reduction in falls.

claims.claim: Hydroxychloroquine prevents COVID-19
claims.basis: Cochrane (Singh 2021): hydroxychloroquine does not prevent infection in exposed adults (trials of about 3,300 people), and pre-exposure trials in health workers found no benefit; the WHO living guideline (2021) and NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines recommend against it for prevention.

claims.claim: Ovarian cancer screening saves lives
claims.basis: USPSTF 2018 grade D against screening healthy women; PLCO (Buys 2011) and UKCTOCS (Jacobs 2016, Menon 2021) found no significant fall in ovarian cancer deaths, and false positives led to unneeded surgery with serious complications. UKCTOCS hints at a possible delayed benefit with one method, so a narrower reading is fair.

claims.claim: Exercising during pregnancy harms the baby
claims.basis: ACOG Committee Opinion 804 (2020) and WHO physical activity guidelines (2020) advise regular exercise in healthy pregnancy; meta-analyses of trials (Davenport 2018, Barakat 2023) find no added risk of miscarriage, preterm birth or fetal death, and less gestational diabetes.

claims.claim: Vertebroplasty relieves pain from spinal compression fractures
claims.basis: Cochrane (Buchbinder 2018, 21 trials): high to moderate-certainty evidence of no clinically important pain relief compared with a sham procedure (Buchbinder 2009 and Kallmes 2009 in NEJM; VERTOS IV, Firanescu 2018). NICE (2013) allows it only for severe ongoing pain after a recent unhealed fracture, so a narrow reading is fair.

claims.claim: Mammograms save lives in women in their 40s
claims.basis: USPSTF 2024 (grade B, biennial screening from age 40) finds a mortality benefit, but it is smaller in the 40s than from 50 on, with many more false positives and some overdiagnosis; the UK Age trial (Duffy 2020) found fewer breast cancer deaths in the first 10 years but not afterwards; Cochrane (Gotzsche 2013) disputes the net benefit.

claims.claim: Fluoride in drinking water lowers children's IQ
claims.basis: National Toxicology Program monograph (2024): moderate confidence that fluoride above 1.5 mg/L is linked to lower IQ in children, but too little data to judge the 0.7 mg/L used in US water; meta-analysis (Taylor 2025, JAMA Pediatrics) agrees at higher levels and calls low-level data limited; CDC and WHO still support fluoridation at recommended levels.

claims.claim: Aspartame causes cancer
claims.basis: IARC (2023) classed aspartame as possibly carcinogenic (group 2B) on limited evidence, mainly liver cancer; JECFA (2023) found no reason to change the acceptable daily intake of 40 mg per kg; NCI says studies show no clear link, so a plain no is also a fair reading.

claims.claim: Breastfeeding prevents childhood obesity
claims.basis: The PROBIT cluster trial (Martin 2017, JAMA Pediatrics) found no effect of breastfeeding promotion on obesity at age 11.5; observational studies and the USDA systematic review (2020) find moderate-certainty lower odds with ever versus never breastfeeding, but residual confounding cannot be excluded.

claims.claim: Medical cannabis relieves chronic pain
claims.basis: NASEM (2017) found substantial evidence that cannabis relieves chronic pain in adults, but Cochrane (Mucke 2018) rated the evidence for neuropathic pain low-quality with benefits outweighed by side effects for many, and the BMJ meta-analysis (Wang 2021) found only small average pain relief, mostly with THC-containing products.

claims.claim: Bone broth heals leaky gut
claims.basis: PubMed search (October 2026) finds no controlled human study of bone broth and gut permeability; a 2019 analysis (Alcock) found broth an unreliable source of collagen building blocks, and the 'benefits' papers rest on nutrient or animal data. Leaky gut is not an established diagnosis.

claims.claim: Rice water makes your hair grow faster
claims.basis: PubMed search (October 2026) finds no clinical trial of rice water for hair growth; a 2023 review of TikTok hair-loss remedies and a 2025 analysis of rice water posts both note the claims lack human evidence.

claims.claim: Beef tallow heals eczema
claims.basis: A 2024 scoping review of tallow on skin (Russell, Cureus) found only comparative, laboratory and animal studies and called for randomized trials; a 2025 analysis of social media tallow claims (J Cosmet Dermatol) found few studies; PubMed (October 2026) shows no controlled human trial in eczema.
